fields.name: source_list
fields.label: Source List
fields.sourceQuote: In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1
fields.notes: THE ONE FIELD THIS PAGE DOCUMENTS WELL, and the single field that resolves all four already-written forward endpoints into this page (dep.g1.061, dep.g2.003, dep.g5g5.050, dep.g5g5.051). Exact field name per the corpus is 'Source List'. validValues is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION AND CORRECTLY SO: the options are the tenant's own List Management lists, so no documented list can enumerate them and inventing any would be a tenant-specific value - forbidden by the blind-build rule. What IS documented is the option's PROVENANCE and a hard cardinality rule. Provenance: the list must already exist in List Management before it can be selected here ('Create the source list, match to Vendor Employee Access.', tools-guides/step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md); admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md states the same as a precondition for the Invoice Payment hierarchy - 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.' Cardinality rule: 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.' (bcaf1f5a) - the shape of the chosen list DICTATES how many Level/Segment Name rows must be created here. Wording drifts by feature: bcaf1f5a says 'In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1'; fb3e6aa2 says 'Select the source list to use to identify the various funding accounts.'; 8b510285 says 'A source list is required to map the hierarchy path segments for use.' Same control, three feature contexts. [MERGE] Cross-lens duplicate 'sourceList' (tables lens) carried the identical sourceFile and identical verbatim sourceQuote and was folded into this single record under the canonical snake_case name; no second node emitted. Both refuters returned disposition keep with verbatimVariantIndex 0, and I re-confirmed grep -F -c = 1 for the sourceQuote and for every quote embedded in these notes. Label MUST stay exactly 'Source List' so the four already-written endpoints dep.g1.061, dep.g2.003, dep.g5g5.050 and dep.g5g5.051 resolve here.

Most likely provisioning/feature-dependent: what the level control offers varies with which feature hierarchy is selected. validValues left EMPTY at field level on purpose so neither reading is silently promoted to the whole page. fieldType 'unknown' because no file states the widget - it may be a fixed display for Employee and a selector for Request. SEPARATELY, 'Level' has a documented DEPTH range of 1..10 for the Invoice Vendor Employee Access source list, attested identically in two import specs ('Level 1 of the source list attached to the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy.' through Level 10, the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b51ca3d.md and vendor-group-mapping-record-type-310-6eb8ffdc.md) - that is IMPORT-RECORD depth, not a value list for this page control, and per instruction I did NOT re-emit the Group 5 Level value set. [REPAIR APPLIED] Defect named by refuter 1 of 2: the procedure-lens and tables-lens variants both set fieldType 'dropdown', which this record's OWN sourceQuote contradicts - 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).' A control the cited file says cannot be changed is not attested as a selectable dropdown. fieldType is therefore 'unknown' (the crosscut lens's own honest value and a legal type here): no corpus file states the widget, and the two documented contexts behave differently - fixed 'Employee' for Invoice Vendor Employee Access (bcaf1f5a) versus an act of setting, 'Set the level to Request.' (admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md, grep -F -c = 1). validValues stays [] and BOTH context-scoped readings plus the contradiction node are kept unreconciled, per the governing constraint. Unresolved internal tension retained: step 5 of bcaf1f5a says the value cannot be changed while step 7 of the same file says 'If you intend to use multi-level named vendor groups (Level 1; Level 2; Level 3) add additional levels and segments now to match.' - so more than one Level row is evidently creatable. Its 'Request' and this page's 'Set the level to Request.' are an ACUTE near-miss: a merge keyed on label+value would fuse two unrelated hierarchy editors. Keeping validValues empty here is what prevents that. grep -F -c for 'Line Item', 'Allocation', 'Country', 'Org Unit', 'Policy Name' and 'Custom 1' all return 0 in BOTH Feature Hierarchies files - none of that value set is attested here.

You have the option of renaming the Custom field in Step 4.' The number of Segment Name rows is not free: it must match the source list's level count (bcaf1f5a, 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.'). [MERGE] Cross-lens duplicate 'segment_name' (procedure and crosscut lenses) carried the identical sourceFile and identical verbatim sourceQuote; folded into this one record under the canonical snake_case name, per refuter 1's direction to prefer these tables-lens notes because they alone carry the documented cardinality rule and the fb3e6aa2 label drift. fields.notes: The selector on the Feature Hierarchies landing screen that picks WHICH named feature hierarchy you are about to edit. validValues is DELIBERATELY EMPTY and that is the correct blind-build answer: NO file in this corpus enumerates the selector's option list. What the corpus gives instead is five feature-hierarchy names each attested in its own separate topic, which is an ATTESTED-NAMES LIST, not a documented option list, and is therefore recorded here in prose rather than promoted into graph values. The five, with their files and verbatim wording: (1) 'Invoice Vendor Employee Access' - 'On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy.' (tools-guides/step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md); (2) 'Invoice Payment' - 'Select the Invoice Payment feature name.' (admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md); (3) 'Invoice Routing' - 'The user first specifies the source list and relevant segments using the Invoice Routing hierarchy in the Feature Hierarchies area.' (tools-guides/create-the-invoice-routing-feature-hierarchy-8b510285.md); (4) 'Payment Authorized Approvers' - '(Optional) Set up the Payment Authorized Approvers hierarchy if you choose to use authorized approvers.' (admin-guides/workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md), written elsewhere as 'Authorized Approver Feature Hierarchy' (admin-guides/user-administrator-fcfd570c.md); (5) 'Cost Object Approver' - 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.' (admin-guides/step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md). A sixth appears in a workflow context: 'By default, the Request Authorized Approver hierarchy uses the Request and Employee fields' (admin-guides/understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md). WHICH OF THESE A GIVEN SITE ACTUALLY OFFERS IS UNDETERMINED - the list is near-certainly provisioning-dependent, since each name is documented only inside the setup guide for the module that consumes it. An automation driver must match the feature name by text, never by ordinal position. This fan-out across four config domains is the structural reason Feature Hierarchies is a SHARED page and not a Workflows or Routing Configuration surface. [REPAIR APPLIED - HIGHEST-SEVERITY GROUNDING DEFECT ON THIS PAGE] As received from the crosscut lens this record carried validValues ['Invoice Vendor Employee Access','Invoice Payment']. BOTH ARE STRIPPED and validValues is now []. Reasons, both refuters concurring: (a) the record cited bcaf1f5a, where grep -F -c 'Invoice Payment' = 0 - that value lives ONLY in admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md ('Select the Invoice Payment feature name.', grep -F -c = 1), a different file; (b) the pair was synthesized from two separate single-feature procedures, i.e. two attested instances, not a documented enumeration - exactly the shape the blind-build rule forbids promoting, and the same failure as the two invented 'Yes' values already deleted from this project; (c) it was internally inconsistent, excluding Invoice Routing, Payment Authorized Approvers and Cost Object Approver which have equal footing, so a driver reading two options where the corpus attests five would conclude three real hierarchies do not exist. NO FILE IN THIS CORPUS ENUMERATES THIS SELECTOR'S OPTIONS - 'Feature Hierarchies' appears in 17 files across both guide dirs and not one lists the selector contents. The five attested names are carried in the prose above as an ATTESTED-NAMES LIST, explicitly NON-EXHAUSTIVE and provisioning-dependent. fieldType repaired from the inferred 'dropbox'-style 'dropdown' to 'unknown': the record's own original notes admitted 'the corpus never states the widget', and bcaf1f5a describes selecting a named row on a list page then clicking Modify Hierarchy - the same select-row-then-Modify pattern as page.group-configurations, not an attested dropdown. sourceQuote widened to the full self-contained sentence (grep -F -c = 1 in bcaf1f5a). [DEDUPE] Survivor of a three-way intra-page duplication - feature_name_selector (procedure lens) and featureHierarchyName (tables lens) are the SAME control, same file, same clause, and all three quotes verify verbatim, so neither drop is a grounding refutation. THE REFUTERS SPLIT ON WHICH NAME SURVIVES: refuter 1 chose feature_name_selector, refuter 2 chose feature_name. I took feature_name because both refuters independently held that 'feature name' is the corpus's OWN wording ('Select the Invoice Payment feature name.', fb3e6aa2, grep -F -c = 1) whereas feature_name_selector's label was a describer's paraphrase - '(feature hierarchy row selection on the Feature Hierarchies page)' - which hard-won rule 7 forbids, and its '_selector' suffix is coined; snake_case also matches source_list / level / segment_name on this page. Refuter 1 authorised this outcome in terms: 'If the merge machinery keeps this record instead of the survivor, it MUST be repaired to validValues [] with the attested names carried in notes only, and fieldType set to unknown.' Done. The tables lens's five-name attestation, which refuter 2 ordered transplanted, is the prose above. [SUB-PAGE] This selector sits on the Feature Hierarchies LANDING screen; Source List, Level and Segment Name are reachable only AFTER Modify Hierarchy, and the corpus NEVER NAMES that editor sub-surface - contrast Accounting Administration, where SAP writes 'Select Modify Hierarchy to display the Account Code Hierarchy for Ledger page.' verifyNotes:
SHAPE: 8 names in (5 KEEP, 3 REPAIR), 7 records out. 5 came through clean, 2 were repaired (level, feature_name), 1 REPAIR-bucket input (feature_name_selector) was moved to dropped as an intra-page duplicate rather than emitted, so no name outside the KEEP/REPAIR lists appears and no name is emitted twice. All 7 names are unique; field names are page-scoped in this graph and I checked the existing 486-field kg-invoice-config.json for every one.

WHAT THE REFUTERS FOUND, AND WHAT I DID.
(1) ZERO QUOTE DEFECTS across all 12 candidates - refuter 1 verified every sourceQuote at grep -F -c >= 1 with verbatimVariantIndex 0 throughout. I re-ran grep -F -c myself on every quote I emit AND on every quote embedded in notes: 26 distinct strings, all returned exactly 1. fromRawHtmlTable=false is justified on both cited files - grep -c '<table' = 0 and the indented-table check grep -cP '^\s+\|' = 0, run rather than assumed.
(2) THE ONE REAL GROUNDING DEFECT, REPAIRED: feature_name carried validValues ['Invoice Vendor Employee Access','Invoice Payment'] while citing bcaf1f5a, where grep -F -c 'Invoice Payment' = 0 - that value lives only in fb3e6aa2. The pair was synthesized from two separate single-feature procedures: two attested instances, not a documented enumeration. STRIPPED to []. This is the same failure mode as the two invented 'Yes' values this project already deleted. The five attested hierarchy names are carried in notes as an explicitly NON-EXHAUSTIVE, provisioning-dependent attested-names list.
(3) LEVEL fieldType REPAIRED from 'dropdown' to 'unknown' - the record's own quote says the value 'cannot be changed', so a selectable dropdown is not attested; and the two documented contexts behave differently. Both readings and the contradiction are kept unreconciled.
(4) THE REFUTERS DISAGREED ON ONE POINT and I am flagging it rather than hiding it: which of the three names for the feature selector survives. Refuter 1 chose feature_name_selector; refuter 2 chose feature_name. Both agreed on the repaired CONTENT (label 'feature name', fieldType 'unknown', validValues []). I took feature_name because both refuters independently held that 'feature name' is SAP's own wording ('Select the Invoice Payment feature name.', fb3e6aa2, count 1) while the alternative's label was a describer's paraphrase - hard-won rule 7 - and because refuter 1 wrote the fallback in terms: if feature_name is kept, repair it to validValues [] and fieldType 'unknown'. Done.
(5) 12 CANDIDATES COLLAPSED TO 7 CONTROLS. Five drops, EVERY ONE pure cross-lens duplication with an identical file and an identical verbatim quote - not one drop is a grounding refutation, and both refuters said so explicitly because a prior run dropped a verbatim twin while keeping a reformatted record. Per both refuters' instructions the losers' better notes were TRANSPLANTED onto the survivors: the five-name attestation onto feature_name, the gate-ordering onto modify_hierarchy_button, the repeatability rule onto new_level_button, the fb3e6aa2 corroboration onto save_button, and the cardinality rule and label drift onto segment_name.

COVERAGE = PARTIAL, AND WHY - STATED BEFORE EXTRACTION AND CONFIRMED AFTER. This is a real page and it is genuinely thin. All 12 candidates cite exactly TWO files totalling ~96 lines: tools-guides/step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md (47 lines) and admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md (49 lines, whose only procedure is its '## Configure Feature Hierarchy' section, read end to end to its last line '8.  Select Save.' to confirm nothing leaked in from the payment-groups surface). The brief predicted 'roughly five' (Source List, Level, Segment Name, the feature-name selector, Modify Hierarchy); all five are present and the only extras are New and Save, both verbatim numbered steps in BOTH documented procedures and both heavily precedented (the built graph carries ~20 'New' and 15 'Save' button nodes, including hierarchy_level_new / segment_new / hierarchy_level_save / segment_save on Accounting Administration's structurally identical hierarchy editor). Trimming to hit the number would have been the defect, not thrift.

THE LOUDEST WARNING FOR WHOEVER MERGES THIS - LABEL HOMONYM COLLISION WITH A BUILT PAGE. page.accounting-administration ALREADY OWNS the same five labels in the same order: modify_hierarchy ('Modify Hierarchy'), segment_name ('Segment Name', 5 values), segment_level ('Level', 3 values), segment_new ('New'), segment_save ('Save') - all on the 'Account Code Hierarchy for Ledger page' from edce1aa5 / d6dfb07b. THESE ARE DISTINCT SURFACES, NOT DOUBLE-FILINGS, and refuter 2 proved it two ways: grep -rln 'Segment Name' over BOTH guide dirs returns EXACTLY TWO files, d6dfb07b and bcaf1f5a - one per page, zero overlap; and grep -rl 'Source List' returns 4 files, none of them an Accounting Administration topic. THE ACUTE NEAR-MISS: Accounting Administration's segment_level enumerates 'Request' and this page's Invoice Payment procedure says 'Set the level to Request.' A merge keyed on label+value would fuse two unrelated hierarchy editors and hand an automation driver the wrong option list. ALL FOUR OF THIS PAGE'S value-bearing fields keep validValues EMPTY, which is what prevents it. I confirmed independently that grep -F -c for 'Line Item', 'Allocation', 'Country', 'Org Unit', 'Policy Name' and 'Custom 1' all return 0 in BOTH Feature Hierarchies files.
